Author’s note: When I started working on acoustics projects as a master’s student, the very first book I picked up was Psychoacoustics.

Hugo Fastl is a distinguished professor of technical acoustics at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). His career and research have had a profound influence on acoustics, particularly on psychoacoustics and audiovisual interaction.

Background

Born in 1944, Hugo Fastl trained in both electrical engineering and music, with the double bass as his main instrument. He completed his music studies at the Munich Academy of Music in 1969 and earned his degree in electrical engineering (Dipl.-Ing.) at TUM in 1970. He went on to receive his doctorate (Dr.-Ing.) in 1974 and his habilitation (Dr.-Ing. habil.) in 1981, spent 1987 as a visiting professor at Osaka University in Japan, and in 1991 was appointed professor of technical acoustics at TUM. This interdisciplinary background has allowed him to bring both technical and artistic perspectives to his acoustics research.

Research areas

Fastl’s research focuses mainly on the following areas:

  • Fundamentals of psychoacoustics

    : the quantitative relationship between acoustic stimuli and auditory perception, for quantities such as loudness, roughness and pitch.

  • Audiovisual interaction

    : how visual information affects the perception of sound, for example how colors, images or scenes influence judgments of loudness.

  • Applications

    : audio communication, noise assessment, sound quality design, the diagnosis and rehabilitation of hearing impairment, audio technology and musical acoustics.

His research makes the point that perceiving sound is not purely a matter of hearing but also involves interaction between the senses, which is especially important in modern applications of acoustics.

Key contributions

Fastl’s work spans many areas. Here are a few of his key findings and achievements:

  • The effect of audiovisual interaction

    : In one study he found that visual stimuli can significantly change perceived loudness. In the experiment, the same sound was rated 15% louder when shown with a red train than with a green one (source: “Audio-visual interactions in loudness evaluation”). Visual cues such as color or scene, in other words, change how we perceive sound, and the effect is especially pronounced in the assessment of traffic noise.

  • Automotive sound quality

    : Fastl’s research has made important contributions to evaluating the sound quality of cars. His 2016 paper “Zur Bedeutung psychoakustischer Größen bei der Beurteilung automotiver Geräusche” (On the significance of psychoacoustic quantities in the assessment of automotive sounds; source: Professoren TUM Fastl) examines the role psychoacoustic parameters play in evaluating vehicle noise. This line of research has helped optimize the sound of car doors and the sound design of electric vehicles, for example by making sure that EVs emit a safe warning sound that complies with EU regulations.

  • A classic textbook

    : Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models, which Fastl co-authored with Eberhard Zwicker, is the authoritative work in the field. The third edition, published in 2007, added a chapter on audiovisual interaction (source: Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models). The book has been described as “an essential source of psychoacoustic knowledge,” has some 4,500 citations on Google Scholar and is widely used in teaching and research.

  • Awards and recognition

    : Fastl’s achievements have earned him a number of international awards, including the European Acoustics Association (EAA) Award for Lifetime Achievements in 2017, the Helmholtz Medal of the German Acoustical Society (DEGA) in 2010 and the Rayleigh Medal of the UK Institute of Acoustics in 2003 (source: Rayleigh Medal for Professor Michael Vorländer). These honors recognize his outstanding contributions to acoustics.

Practical applications

Fastl’s research has found practical use in many fields, especially in the automotive industry and in hearing health:

  • Automotive sound design

    : His research has helped improve the sound quality of cars. In a 2018 interview, for example, he discussed personalized sound design for electric vehicles that keeps them both safe and pleasant (source: “Prof. Dr. Hugo Fastl: Der personalisierte Sound des Elektroautos,” or “The personalized sound of the electric car”). Electric vehicles must emit specific sounds to comply with EU rules that took effect in 2019, so that pedestrians do not overlook a car simply because it is quiet.

  • Hearing rehabilitation

    : His work also extends to the diagnosis and rehabilitation of hearing impairment, for example the development of a background noise for speech audiometry (“A background noise for speech audiometry”).

  • Noise control

    : Fastl’s work has made important contributions to assessing and controlling noise in everyday environments, such as the loudness assessment of traffic noise, helping to design quieter cities.

Impact on society and culture

Fastl’s research reaches beyond academia into everyday life. His work on audiovisual interaction, for example, shows how visual information changes the way we perceive sound, which matters a great deal in urban planning and in the entertainment industry, such as film sound design. His interdisciplinary background in electrical engineering and music has also let him bring technology and art together, particularly in musical acoustics, for instance in studying how different tuning standards (such as 432 Hz versus 440 Hz) affect the perception of music.

Summary

Hugo Fastl is a pioneer in acoustics. His research on psychoacoustics and audiovisual interaction has laid important theoretical groundwork for automotive sound design, hearing rehabilitation and noise control. His book Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models is widely regarded as a classic of the field and has shaped acoustics teaching and research around the world. His work shows how complex the perception of sound is, and how vision and the other senses shape what we hear.
